what_happened: Seeding a fresh review worktree's .lake/build by 'cp -a' from another worktree silently produced a FALSE-GREEN build: Lake's per-module .trace files record the ABSOLUTE source path of the worktree they were built in, and Lake re-hashes that recorded path rather than the current project's file. Every module whose source differed between the two worktrees (including FormalSystem/Semantics/PointTransport.lean, the file under review) was therefore judged up to date and never rebuilt. Detected only because a '#check at_def' probe reported the new theorem as an unknown identifier after a build that had reported 3006/3006 green. Remedy: wipe .lake/build and rebuild from scratch (.lake/packages is a symlink to the main repo and is safe to share).

lake-build-guard.sh's --dir DIR flag resolves the project root for locking and result-record paths ONLY; it never chdirs, so the wrapped 'lake' invocation runs in the CALLER'S cwd. Invoking 'bash .claude/scripts/lake-build-guard.sh build --dir <worktree> -- build --wfail' from the main repository therefore builds the MAIN REPOSITORY and reports a green result that says nothing about the worktree under review. Detected when a '#check at_def' probe in the worktree reported the PR's new theorem as an unknown identifier after a 3006/3006 green run. Remedy: cd into the worktree first and invoke the guard from there (--dir is then redundant).

Falsifying the 'At is now usable' claim took eight one-example probe files compiled individually with 'lake env lean', each isolating one tactic line. The at_def-omitted control (simp only [TruthEnv.T, PlusTruth.allFuture_iff] -> 'simp made no progress') and the generic-former control (at_def reported UNUSED) together pinned down exactly where at_def is load-bearing and where it is not -- a distinction the shipped test alone cannot show, since it bundles all three lemmas into one simp set. Cheap, reusable pattern for auditing any 'lemma X makes Y usable' claim.

Dispatch description's per-file deltas for the new commit do not match measurement. Description: PointTransport.lean +7/-2, TemporalRulesTest.lean +72, PointTransportTest.lean +35. Measured via 'git diff --numstat c6cd983b7 b2eb3ac0b': 7/2, 65/7 and 34/1 respectively. Only PointTransport.lean matches; the two test files' figures are overstated on additions and omit the deletions (the someFuture_bind/somePast_bind rows were rewritten in place, not added beside). No effect on the verdict.

Plan's zero-goal Lean Challenge declaration was confirmed mechanically rather than asserted: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh 990 <root> --dry-run reported the marker recognized and Goals naming no identifiers, and validate-artifact.sh passed with 0 warnings. Cost one cheap command each and removed the usual authoring-time uncertainty about whether a lean4 plan with no theorem deliverable is well-formed.

Phase 2's first draft of pr11-approval.md landed at 64 lines against the plan's 35-55 line Scope Hypothesis. Cut to 57 by trimming the status.typ count enumeration, the iffTransport_rev coverage clause and the opening/closing; no content the plan required was dropped. The hypothesis's stated comparison basis (pr7-approval.md, 21 lines) is misleading because that file is unwrapped prose while pr11-comment.md wraps at ~95 chars over 45 lines.

Correction to the preceding scope-estimate entry: the trimmed pr11-approval.md is 61 lines, not 57. It stays 6 lines above the plan's 35-55 Scope Hypothesis and no further cut was made, because every remaining paragraph is required by a Phase 2 checklist item and the only way to reach 55 would have been to rewrap at a wider column, which games the metric rather than cutting substance. Recorded as a knowing overshoot.

Phase 4's scoped discharge (verify-touched.sh) reported 84 passed / 1 failed (NEW) / 10 skipped over 95 suites. The single failure is tests/test-deploy-baseline-lib.sh, case 'control: a genuinely matching warm-cache entry was expected to skip gate 1 but did not' -- the standing, environment-specific defect in verify-deploy.sh's gate-cache warm-path logic already confirmed twice in isolated scratch directories. Not attributable to this task: task 990's modified_files contain no .claude/** and no .lean path. verify-touched.sh selected 91 suites because it derives touched paths from the whole working tree plus the committed diff against its own determined base, which under this multi-task batch includes sibling tasks' and prior sessions' changes rather than only this task's four files.

The plan's Phase 1 head-re-confirmation gate and its pinned sha made this dispatch almost mechanical: the head was byte-identical at both probes (09:45:17Z and 09:50:58Z), CI was still green on it, and zero contributor comments had arrived, so the research dispatch's measurement transferred intact and no Lean work, worktree or build was needed. Separating 'measure the verdict' (research) from 'write the prose' (implement) cost one gh probe to validate instead of a re-measurement.
